revise.summary: I revised content/lessons/02-context-window.md against the 1.3.1 SKILL.md files, the Claude Code docs, the repo and the video transcripts. The Site story is now built only from repo facts: the old main-flow Lesson at d21fc2c (no /clear while grilling, /to-spec and /to-tickets ran; /implement-spec helpers in worktrees), the old prototype Lesson (only /prototype typed, code kept on the prototype/lesson-page branch) and .scratch/course-rewrite/HANDOFF.md from commit 629eae0. Everything only a session log backed is cut: clock times, the /setup-matt-pocock-skills then /clear sequence, 380k, the idle compaction from 247k to 31k, and "never typed /compact or /handoff". The body's /context table no longer claims to be this site's build, and it no longer has a made-up "Total used" row. In the Final test, why-big-window and predict-context-growth are gone. In their place, read-context-rows checks that the reader can use /context and spot the signs, and spot-handoff-file covers what a handoff file carries. In all four spot- questions every option now has the same "X should…" form, which removes the wording tell. Other changes: the /tdd Scene is fixed, /handoff is described as a summary, the 2025 video claim says only what Matt said, question 1 of the tree and the cheat sheet now agree, terms are defined at first use, and the Try it steps are reordered so /compact runs on a full window. Both gates pass.
fixed: HIGH (dropped first run, lesson-specific): spot- wording tell. In spot-rule-in-chat, spot-louder-rule, spot-compact-first and the new spot-handoff-file, all four options now share one form ('Sam/He/She/It should…'), and the right answer is never the longest option by either measure.

quiz.where: Final test (lines 333-453), against goal 3 (line 16: "choose between continuing, `/clear`, `/handoff`, a subagent and `/compact` at a Phase boundary, in Matt's order")
quiz.problem: No Final test question has continuing as its right answer. The only continue options are distractors with the same bait: "Keep going: 90k is well inside a 1M window" (line 367) and "Keep going; most of the 1M window is still free" (line 373). A reader who has learned "continuing is always wrong" passes, which is the opposite of the Lesson's point that continuing comes first. Only the Checkpoint continue-first (which never counts) tests question 1. This was raised as a low last round and is still unfixed.
quiz.evidence: Final test right answers: Messages, subagent, /clear, /compact, /handoff, CLAUDE.md, shrink the window, /clear, point to the spec, handoff detour. Line 155: "That's the price, and why continuing comes first." PHASE-BOUNDARIES.md:21: "Continue costs nothing and loses nothing, so rule it out before anything else." Writing guide line 119: "Every goal gets at least one Final test question".
quiz.fix:
Rewrite spot-compact-first so that continuing is the right answer, using a Phase pair other than the Checkpoint's grilling-to-build. Clear-over-compact stays covered by scenario-next-ticket. Lengths 49/57/50/53, so the right answer is neither longest nor shortest:
```test spot-compact-first
Ana finishes building a search box at 60k tokens. Next she'll check it by hand with the agent, a short job. She types `/compact` first, "to start QA clean". Spot the mistake.
- [ ] She should `/clear` instead, for a cleaner start.
  > QA still needs what the build did. Clearing loses the why for good, and question 1 already says yes.
- [ ] She should have compacted mid-build, before it got heavy.
  > Compacting mid-Phase makes the agent lose the thread, and 60k was never heavy.
- [ ] She should `/handoff` instead, so nothing is lost.
  > Nothing is travelling, and a handoff file is a summary too.
- [x] She should carry on in this session and start QA now.
  > Right. A short QA fits easily in the Smart zone left at 60k, so question 1 says yes. Continuing costs nothing and keeps the build firsthand.
```

quiz.evidence: Line 82 (body): "Pasting the ignored instruction again, in capitals, adds tokens to a window that already holds too many." Line 408 (prompt): "He pastes the rule again, in capitals, three times in a row." Line 415: "He should paste it a fourth time, at the very start of his message." Writing guide line 118: "Use a fresh situation ... not the body's own example sentence."
quiz.fix:
Replace it with a fresh adding move (the Common mistakes' "Pasting big files") and real misconceptions as distractors. Lengths 55/49/58/52:
```test spot-louder-rule
Deep into a long session, Raj's agent keeps naming files the old way, though he set a new rule early on. So he pastes in the team's whole 40-page style guide, "so it can't miss it". Spot the mistake.
- [x] He should shrink the window at the next Phase boundary.
  > Right. Past the Smart zone, more tokens make it worse. Start a smaller window at a boundary, and put the rule in `CLAUDE.md`.
- [ ] He should switch to a model with a bigger window.
  > Window size isn't the limit; the Smart zone is. A bigger window just holds more dumb zone.
- [ ] He should have the agent repeat the rule after every edit.
  > Still adding tokens. The model can see the rule; its attention is spread too thin to keep hold of it.
- [ ] He should let auto-compact run first, then paste it.
  > Auto-compact fires only when the window is nearly full, far into the dumb zone. Waiting for it means more work done badly.
```

quiz.problem: The prompt names the problem (the copied spec), and only the right option mentions the spec, so it echoes the prompt. The other options are weak. "Also paste in the whole conversation" (a) makes a file the prompt already calls too long even longer. "Leave out what's next" (d) has nothing to do with the length problem. A reader can answer by matching words, without knowing what the file should carry.
quiz.evidence: Prompt line 432: "It's long, because it copies in the whole 300-line spec, word for word." Options: a "It should also paste in the whole conversation, so nothing is lost.", b [x] "It should point to the spec by its path.", c "It should drop its suggested-skills section to save space.", d "It should leave out what's next, since the colleague decides that." The key itself is right: productivity/handoff/SKILL.md:12 "Do not duplicate content already captured in other artifacts (specs, plans, ADRs, issues, commits, diffs). Reference them by path or URL instead."
quiz.fix:
Keep the prompt and make every option about the spec. Lengths 44/53/62/56:
- [ ] It should boil the spec down to a paragraph.
  > Still a copy, just a lossy one. The spec already lives in its own file, so the handoff should point there.
- [x] It should point to the spec by its path, not copy it.
  > Right. A handoff file refers to specs, tickets and commits by path or link instead of copying them, so it stays short.
- [ ] It should keep the spec and drop its suggested-skills section.
  > That section tells the next agent which Skills to load. The copied spec is what makes the file long.
- [ ] It should keep the spec and cut the summary of the work.
  > What's in flight, why and what's next is the heart of the file. The copied spec is the part that doesn't belong.
